messages:
alert-bot: DETECTION: Suspicious KMS Decrypt activity from service-account 'svc-analytics-prod' in us-west1, 3x baseline in last 5m. Rule: kms-decrypt-anomaly
Jordan: seeing the alert. grabbing logs now. any change events in IAM?
Priya: looking at audit logs -> found a recent IAM binding change at 1803004200: role 'roles/cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' granted to svc-analytics-prod with source=console.
Mateo: confirmed, I can see the console auth entry. IP is unfamiliar: 54.33.122.7 (not in allowlist).
Lina: tagging this as potential privilege escalation. Start containment: revoke temporary creds + remove binding. Sam, can you do RBAC rollback?
Sam: on it. running: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-analytics-prod@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` then `gcloud iam roles remove-iam-policy-binding`. Will post cmds.
Sam: removed binding `roles/cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` from svc-analytics-prod at 1803004385. Also disabled the service account key (if any) and added org policy deny in a temp rule.
Priya: great. I'm triggering a KMS rotation for the affected key-ring envelope key (staging rotation path) and enabling object-level audit export to BigQuery for deeper queries. Command: `gcloud kms keys versions destroy --location=us-west1 --keyring=prod-ring --key=envelope-key --version=latest --quiet` (rotating per playbook).
Mateo: network folks, can we block 54.33.122.7 at the edge ACLs?
Jordan: already pushed a deny to cloud firewall and WAF for that IP. Noting for evidence.
Lina: Collect evidence: stackdriver exports, console session history, all `gcloud` audit logs for svc-analytics-prod, and snapshot the KMS audit trail. Save to incident bucket: gs://incidents/1803004321-evidence/
Priya: copying logs now to that bucket. Also creating a hash of the exported logs: `sha256sum` stored as `logs.sha256`.
Sam: opened INC-2026-1803 in our tracker with severity=P2 until we confirm if data exposure occurred. Assigned to Priya and Mateo for triage.
Priya: initial triage: decrypt events were limited to 3 objects, unknown whether plaintext pulled out of infra. I'm scanning downstream storage access patterns now.
Mateo: checking microservice telemetry. svc-analytics-prod made grpc calls to analytics-pipeline for those timestamps; pipeline writes to gs://analytics-processed. Granting read checks for those objects now.
Jordan: FYI adding exec: @Lina will lead comms with legal/infosec. Notify customers if confirmed.
Lina: notified legal and compliance via email thread, attaching incident artifacts. Preparing short comms template.
Sam: taking snapshot of current IAM state and exporting via `gcloud iam roles list` + `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` to the incident bucket.
Priya: next steps for oncall handoff: collect questions for next shift, confirm rotation complete, and make sure temporary deny rule remains for svc-analytics-prod.
Jordan: Handoff checklist to next oncall (paste into ticket):
- binary evidence: gs://incidents/1803004321-evidence/exports.tar.gz
- actions taken: revoked role (1803004385), disabled keys, firewall block (1803004400), KMS rotation triggered (1803004430)
- items pending: full object access audit, confirm if plaintext exfil, confirm key re-enablement policy
- contacts: Priya (sec-eng), Mateo (infra), Lina (compliance)
Priya: I'll continue scans for 45m, then will hand to Mateo if still open. If any finds, ping with `@Jordan` and `@Lina`.
Mateo: I'll own remediation tasks overnight if required.
Lina: thanks team. Logging this thread into postmortem bucket and will prep a timeline. Handoff to next oncall at 1803004890 — Jordan signing off from active command. :white_check_mark:
